script: A company made women paint watch dials with radium paint, and here is what happened. In the 1910s and 1920s, US Radium Corporation hired young women to paint glow-in-the-dark numbers using radium based paint. Workers were taught to point their brushes with their lips to keep a fine tip, ingesting small amounts of radium each time. Over the following years, many of the painters developed serious bone and jaw conditions. Several workers eventually died from complications linked to radium exposure. Five of the surviving workers filed a lawsuit against the company in 1927. The case was settled, and it became a significant moment in the history of workplace safety regulation in the United States. A company made women paint with radium, and the case that followed changed how factories were regulated.
